Code § 1950.6)","requirement":"A landlord or agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only to cover actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information on the applicant (e.g., tenant screening or credit report costs) plus the reasonable value of time spent, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjustable annually with CPI from Jan. 1, 1998). No fee may be charged if the landlord knows or should know no unit is or will soon be available. A fee may be charged only if the landlord offers either (A) a first-come, first-qualified screening process with written screening criteria provided with the application, no fee charged unless the application is actually considered (inadvertent concurrent collection must be refunded within 7 days or may be applied to another unit at the applicant's option), or (B) return of the entire fee to any applicant not selected, within 7 days of selecting an applicant or 30 days after the application was submitted, whichever is first. The landlord must give a itemized receipt (personally, by mail, or by agreed email), return any unused portion of the fee if no reference check or credit report is obtained, and provide a copy of the credit report to the applicant within 7 days of receiving it. Landlords may accept a reusable screening report under Section 1950.1.","key_value":"$30 per applicant maximum (CPI-adjustable annually); refund within 7 days (or 30 days from submission, whichever first, under option B)","coverage_conditions":"Applies to landlords (owners of residential rental property) and their agents charging applicants (including guarantors or cosignors) for residential rental units statewide.","exemptions":"Does not preempt provisions or regulations governing collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.
